title: It used to be a simple question and answer site.
content: Now, I feel like it’s used for writing. I mean, Google can answer just about any question you might have. And can do so quicker and often more accurately than Quora ever could. But Quora can, at times, provide a little more flair. And at times, better writing.

title: Why has Quora lost its popularity a little over the years
content: Reddit is gonna meet the same fate in a few years' time. The site is already getting a heavy influx of bots so you can't trust the opinion on newer threads and Reddit has started becoming anti-user friendly due to the company going public.

title: Is Quora a good platform? Are people here genuinely serious about giving questions and answers?
content:
Qurora is the only platform of its kind that I know of. Even the terrible Yahoo Answers that died in 2021 was not in the same class. Yes, Quora is a good platform. Yes, the people who seriously engage with it are interested in quality. I believe real Quorans are willing to spend their own effort to be respectful of people on the other side of a question, whether they are asking or answering.

But 90% “genuine questions and answers”, as another responder estimates? I think the number is much lower, and declining. The inane questions, the obvious inflamatory questions, the semi-literate questions, the questions that beg a simple Google search — I have a hard time believing they come from actual humans typing, or at least typing with some their brain engaged. Someone throws all those garbage questions out there. If it is not the platform itself, the platform is guilty of not using its software to filter them out, or to de-prioritize the accounts that create them.

Obviously one fellow Quoran thinks there may be “7 or 8 year olds” out there. Hate to be the bearer of bad news, but those are adults or older teens with either the IQ of a 7 or 8 year old or the disposition of a child. Almost every engaged young Quoran is more literate than 90 percent of their school peers or they wouldn’t be here.

I don’t know how to save Quora from what I consider an increaing wave of spam questions and spam answers (like one-sentence ‘answers’ that help the person build statistical volume). The advent of the owner’s efforts to insert an element of pay for participants is contemporaneous with the decline in quality at Quora. In the old days, people tried to craft good questions and good answers because they WANTED to, because the act of doing so gave them a personal reward.

We might look at how online news destroyed itself. When the Fairness Doctrine was removed and the broadcasters started to demand that news shows MAKE MONEY, the news shows went to hell. In place of Edward R. Murrow and Walter Cronkite, the owners got a combination of sensationalism, simplistic headlines-only reporting, and politically biased, audience-dictated ‘news’. Platforms like Quora would be better off ignoring us Quorans and just placing ads around our questions and answers. And if they are ‘helping’ by generating a huge volume of duplicate, dumb, and incindiary questions, stop.
